cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: The Odyssey tells the story of Odysseus's ten-year journey home (nostos) from the Trojan War

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Odysseus's key qualities: cunning, eloquence, endurance, bravery, curiosity and leadership

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Unlike Achilles (who chose glory and early death), Odysseus chooses survival and homecoming

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Odysseus's name means 'man of pain' or 'trouble' — his suffering is central to his identity

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: He invented the Trojan Horse, demonstrating his preference for cunning over brute force

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: His encounter with Polyphemus shows both his cleverness (the 'Nobody' trick) and his fatal flaw (revealing his true name)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Odysseus is not a perfect hero — he can be arrogant, reckless and deceitful

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: His disguise as a beggar upon returning to Ithaca shows his mastery of deception and patience

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Penelope's faithfulness and cunning (unraveling the shroud) mirrors Odysseus's own intelligence

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: Telemachus's coming-of-age journey in Books 1-4 parallels his father's heroism

cards.front: Recall a key point about Odysseus the Hero
cards.back: The Odyssey explores what it means to be a hero in peacetime, not just in war
